    """Check if a (non-parameterized) type is a `Sequence`, `Set` or `Mapping` subclass.

    def set_error_reporter(
        self, reporter: Callable[[Any, Exception, dict[str, Any], bool], None] | None
    ) -> None:
        """Set a callable to be notified of exceptions raised while processing requests.

        The reporter makes it possible to observe every exception that is
        passed to the app's error handling, for example in order to log it, or
        to send it to an error tracker. Only one reporter can be set; calling
        this method again replaces the previously set reporter.

        The reporter is invoked before the matching error handler (see also
        :meth:`~.add_error_handler`) for every exception, including instances
        of :class:`~.HTTPError` and :class:`~.HTTPStatus`, regardless of
        whether it was raised while routing the request, in middleware or
        the responder, or while rendering the response body. For
        example::

            def report_error(req, ex, params, handled):
                if not handled or not isinstance(ex, falcon.HTTPError):
                    logger.error('Error in %s', req.path, exc_info=ex)

            app.set_error_reporter(report_error)

        If an error handler re-raises the same exception object, it is not
        reported again. An :class:`~.HTTPError` or :class:`~.HTTPStatus` raised
        from an error handler is reported as handled, and any other exception
        raised by an error handler or the error serializer is reported as
        unhandled before it propagates to the application server. An
        exception preventing the response from being started (such as an
        invalid ``resp.status``) is reported as unhandled too.

                ``True`` if an error handler matches the type of the
                exception, or ``False`` if none does, and the exception is
                going to propagate to the application server.

        .. versionadded:: 4.3
        """
'''
